root.label: Implicit conversions
root.note: A fixed pipeline of standard conversions, optionally around exactly one user-defined conversion.

children.label: Standard sequence slots
children.note: At most one conversion from each of four ordered slots.

children.label: Value transformation
children.note: Lvalue-to-rvalue, array-to-pointer or function-to-pointer, at most one.

children.label: Type change
children.note: One promotion, arithmetic, pointer, pointer-to-member or boolean conversion.

children.label: Function pointer (C++17)
children.note: A pointer to a noexcept function converts to a pointer to a throwing one, not back.

children.label: Qualification
children.note: Adds const or volatile below the top level, last in the sequence.

children.label: Promotion vs conversion
children.note: Both change the type, but promotions rank better in overload resolution.

children.label: Promotions
children.note: Only narrow integers to int or unsigned int, and float to double.

children.label: short to long
children.note: A conversion, so f(long) and f(double) are ambiguous for a short.

children.label: Floating to integer
children.note: Truncates toward zero; undefined if the result does not fit.

children.label: Boolean conversion
children.note: Zero and null become false; it beats any user-defined conversion.

children.label: Pointer conversions
children.note: Null pointer constants, void pointers and derived-to-base.

children.label: Null pointer constant
children.note: Integer literal zero or a std::nullptr_t prvalue; false and const int zero are not (C++11).

children.label: To void*
children.note: Any object pointer converts to cv void*; void* never converts back implicitly.

children.label: Derived to base
children.note: Needs an accessible, unambiguous base; the address may change; null stays null.

children.label: Narrowing
children.note: A lossy implicit conversion that is banned only in certain contexts.

children.label: What narrows
children.note: Float to int, wide to narrow, int to float, and pointer to bool since C++20.

children.label: Constant exception
children.note: A constant expression whose value fits is not narrowing, except float to int.

children.label: Banned in braces
children.note: Every form of list-initialization rejects narrowing; C++20 parenthesized aggregates allow it.

children.label: Converted constants
children.note: Template arguments, case labels, array bounds and noexcept(...) reject narrowing.

children.label: Contextual bool
children.note: Conditions and logical operators convert as if direct-initializing a bool.

children.label: Explicit is allowed
children.note: explicit operator bool works in if, !, && and ?: but not in bool b = x.

children.label: P1401 (C++23)
children.note: static_assert and if constexpr accept narrowing to bool; noexcept(...) does not.

children.label: Requires-clauses
children.note: Atomic constraints are not converted and must have type bool exactly.

children.label: User-defined step
children.note: A constructor or conversion function, applied at most once implicitly.

children.label: Shape
children.note: Standard sequence, then one user-defined conversion, then another standard sequence.

children.label: No chaining
children.note: const char* to std::string to Name is two steps, so Name n = "Ada" fails.

children.label: Direct init escapes
children.note: Name n("Ada") calls the constructor, leaving only one conversion for its argument.
